definition: Clamor means a loud, continuous outcry or noise of many voices.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word clamor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know clamor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By the second week of the bread shortage, the clamor outside the bakery started before the ovens did.
A murmur sits far below a clamor — voices kept so low that no single word survives the trip across the room, where a clamor is many voices raised and insisting.
Bedlam goes further than clamor — a clamor is loud voices demanding something; bedlam is the room gone past demands into pure chaos.

An uproar is a sudden burst of loud commotion — shock, laughter, or anger boiling over — with no particular demand in it. A clamor is loud and wants something: many voices insisting until they are answered. A courtroom erupts into an uproar; a crowd keeps up a clamor for lower fares.

An outcry is the public's protest at something felt to be wrong, and it can live in headlines and petitions as easily as in raised voices. A clamor is always heard — continuous, many-voiced, and demanding. An outcry says this was wrong; a clamor keeps shouting for what it wants.

A hubbub is the mixed, busy noise of a crowd going about its own business — market stalls, a hotel lobby — asking for nothing. A clamor has a spine of demand in it: the voices are loud together because they want something and mean to be answered.
